gaps.line: For his first month inside, Andy kept his head ___ and spoke to nobody.
Brooks simply could not ___ it on the outside.
The Warden ruled the prison with an ___ fist.
Tommy let ___ that he knew who had really killed Andy's wife.
The Warden's money was ___ through a false identity.

quiz.q: Why does the Warden have Tommy killed?
options: Tommy could prove Andy's innocence and expose the Warden
Tommy tried to escape with Red
Tommy stole money from the Warden
quiz.why: Tommy's story would reopen Andy's case and put the Warden's money, and his control over Andy, at risk.

quiz.q: Why does Andy write a letter to the state legislature every week?
options: To get books and money for a prison library
To ask for a shorter sentence
quiz.why: He writes for years until the state finally sends money and boxes of books for the library.

quiz.q: What finally makes Red leave for Mexico?
options: Andy's letter and the money under the black rock
An order from the parole board
quiz.why: The letter gives him a promise to keep, and the money gives him a way to break the habit of staying put.

quotes.quote: I hope the Pacific is as blue as it has been in my dreams.
quotes.note: Red's last letter, after he decides to follow Andy south.

quotes.quote: Brooks was here.
quotes.note: Carved into the beam of the halfway house, and the saddest three words in the film.

truefalse.s: Andy works in the prison laundry before he is moved to the library.
The story is narrated by Red, not by Andy.
Andy asks Red for a rock hammer in the first weeks of his sentence.
Andy escapes on a snowy winter night.
truefalse.fix: He escapes on a rainy night with thunder, crawling out through the sewer pipe.

truefalse.s: Red finds Andy's money under a white rock near Buxton.
truefalse.fix: The rock is black, the piece of volcanic rock Andy describes in his letter.

truefalse.s: Tommy is killed in a fight with another prisoner.
truefalse.fix: He is shot by a guard on the Warden's orders, and the death is reported as an escape attempt.

shortAnswers.q: Red describes terrible events in a calm, almost gentle voice. Why does the film give him that voice instead of an angry one?
shortAnswers.model: A calm voice makes the horror sound ordinary and remembered, which is how prison changes a man; it also earns our trust, so we believe him when he finally speaks about hope.

shortAnswers.q: Why does the film show the parole board three times, with almost the same questions each time?
shortAnswers.model: The repetition shows that the system wants a performance of regret rather than the truth, and Red only gets out when he stops performing.

shortAnswers.q: The Warden calls himself a man of God and keeps a Bible by his desk. Why does the film make him quote scripture?
shortAnswers.model: It exposes the gap between the words he uses in public and the money he hides; the Bible that hides the hammer makes the hypocrisy literal.

shortAnswers.q: Red says people have to get busy living. Why does the film give that line to Andy but the last word to Red?
shortAnswers.model: Andy's line is a challenge, but Red is the one who has to act on it, so the film ends with the change it has been describing for twenty years.

gaps.line: My game, my ___, my rules.
Lionel refused to ___ down to a duke.
The doctors had no idea how to ___ with a stammer.
Lionel caught Bertie ___ guard with a question about his childhood.
David chose to walk ___ from the throne for the woman he loved.

quiz.q: Why does Lionel insist on calling the Duke Bertie?
options: He believes the stammer grows out of fear of authority
He wants to be paid more
He has forgotten the Duke's title
quiz.why: Lionel is sure Bertie stammers worse when he is frightened of the person he is speaking to, so he removes the distance.

quiz.q: What surprises Bertie at the end of his first session?
options: He hears himself read aloud without stammering
Lionel gives him a written cure
He is offered a place at Oxford
quiz.why: Lionel records him reading Shakespeare with music playing, and the recording proves that his voice works.

quiz.q: Who stands beside Bertie while he delivers the broadcast?
quiz.why: Lionel is in the room, mouthing the words with him, which is why the long speech holds together.

quotes.quote: My game, my turf, my rules.
quotes.note: Lionel's terms for the therapy, set out in the first session.

quotes.quote: I'm going to call you Bertie.
quotes.note: His refusal to use the title, which shocks the Duke more than any exercise.

truefalse.s: Lionel records Bertie reading at their first meeting.
Bertie's older brother David becomes king before him.
The final speech is broadcast in 1939, when Britain goes to war.
Lionel is a Harley Street doctor with a medical degree.
truefalse.fix: Lionel is an Australian speech therapist with no formal qualifications.

truefalse.s: Bertie meets Lionel for the first time at Wembley Stadium.
truefalse.fix: His wife Elizabeth arranges a visit to Lionel's consulting room in Harley Street.

truefalse.s: David gives up the throne because he is too ill to rule.
truefalse.fix: He abdicates so that he can marry Wallis Simpson, a divorced American.

shortAnswers.q: Lionel swears first and tells Bertie that he may swear too. Why does the film make swearing part of the treatment?
shortAnswers.model: Because fluent swearing proves that Bertie's voice works when he stops monitoring himself, so the film can show that the problem is fear rather than his mouth.

shortAnswers.q: Why does the film keep cutting to the microphone and to the faces in the room during the final speech?
shortAnswers.model: The close-ups show that a radio speech is made of small breaths and looks, so we see the effort behind a voice that sounds calm.

shortAnswers.q: Bertie says he is a naval officer rather than a king. What does that tell us about how he sees himself?
shortAnswers.model: He measures himself against a job where he knew he was competent, and the crown feels like a role he was given rather than one he earned.

shortAnswers.q: Whose version of Bertie do you trust: the court's, which treats him as fragile, or Lionel's, which treats him as capable?
shortAnswers.model: Lionel's, because he is the only person who tests Bertie instead of protecting him, and the broadcast proves that the test was right.

gaps.line: Eduardo was slowly ___ out of his own company.
Eduardo put up the ___ money when the site was only an idea.
gaps.hint: the first money for a new business

gaps.line: Mark refused to ___ an inch during the deposition.
Both sides wanted to ___ a settlement before the trial.
Mark managed to rub the twins up the wrong ___ in one meeting.

quiz.q: Why does Mark build FaceMash on the night Erica breaks up with him?
options: He is angry and wants to lash out at the students around him
He is helping the twins with their site
He is finishing a class project
quiz.why: The site is built in anger and drink, and it turns the evening's humiliation into something the whole campus can vote on.

quiz.q: Why does Eduardo freeze the company bank account?
options: He wants Mark to answer him about the new shares
He is stealing the company's money
He wants to sell the company to Google
quiz.why: Mark stops answering him, so Eduardo uses the only power he has left to force a conversation.

quiz.q: What does Sean's arrest at the party show the investors?
options: That he is brilliant but unreliable
That he owns most of the company
That he has never met Mark
quiz.why: The party and the arrest make him a risk to the company's image just as the serious money arrives.

quotes.quote: The internet isn't written in pencil, Mark. It's written in ink.
quotes.note: Erica's warning about what he has written about her online, and what cannot be taken back.

quotes.quote: I'm not a bad guy.
quotes.note: His line to the lawyer after the depositions, and the claim the film spends two hours testing.

truefalse.s: Mark builds FaceMash after Erica breaks up with him in a bar.
Eduardo is the first person to put money into the company.
The Winklevoss twins row for Harvard.
Mark is a student at Stanford when the site begins.
truefalse.fix: He is a Harvard student in 2003, and the site starts in his dormitory.

truefalse.s: Eduardo's share of the company is diluted to thirty percent.
truefalse.fix: It is diluted to 0.03 per cent, while the others keep their shares.

truefalse.s: The twins ask Mark to build their site before he creates FaceMash.
truefalse.fix: They approach him after FaceMash, because they have seen what he can build.

shortAnswers.q: Why does the film tell the same story three times, in two depositions and in flashback?
shortAnswers.model: Each version serves the person telling it, so the film makes us compare them instead of trusting a narrator; truth becomes something the audience has to assemble.

shortAnswers.q: Mark says he is not a bad guy. Why does the film let him say that and then show us the depositions?
shortAnswers.model: The line is a defence rather than a fact: the film lets him claim it and then shows the friends he lost, so we judge the claim against the evidence.

shortAnswers.q: Sean speaks in slogans. Why does Mark listen to him and not to Eduardo?
shortAnswers.model: Sean sells a future Mark wants, while Eduardo asks him to be careful; the film shows that flattery is more persuasive than friendship.

shortAnswers.q: What is the film really saying about who gets credit for an idea?
shortAnswers.model: It suggests that credit goes to whoever is in the room when the thing is built and to whoever can afford the lawyers, not to whoever thought of it first.

gaps.line: Jules could not bring herself to ___ over the company to a stranger.
Ben knew the office inside ___ within a week.
The company was growing by ___ and bounds.
Jules was spread too ___ to notice what her team needed.
gaps.hint: not enough of her to go round

gaps.line: Jules ___ off the meeting with the investors at the last minute.

quiz.q: Why does Jules first suggest that Ben ask for a transfer?
options: She thinks an intern she cannot use makes her look bad
She has no budget for an intern
quiz.why: She explains that he was assigned to her to set an example, and she cannot see a real job for him.

quiz.q: What makes Jules change her mind about Ben?
options: He quietly tidies a desk nobody asked him to touch
He complains to the human resources team
quiz.why: The clean desk is the first proof that he notices what everyone else walks past, and she starts giving him real work.

quiz.q: Why does Ben agree to break into Jules's mother's house?
options: Jules needs an email deleted before her mother reads it
He wants to meet Jules's mother
Davis asks him for a favour
quiz.why: Jules has sent an email to the wrong person, and Ben organises the raid because he can see how frightened she is.

quotes.quote: I'm loyal, I'm trustworthy, and I'm good in a crisis.
quotes.note: From his application video, and the sentence that gets him the internship.

quotes.quote: I am not so fun to work for.
quotes.note: Her warning in their first two-minute meeting, which is both honest and a way of keeping him away.

truefalse.s: Ben applies with a video instead of a cover letter.
Ben spent forty years at a company that printed phone books.
Nobody at the company has a private office, not even the founder.
Ben is sixty-five when he starts the internship.
truefalse.fix: He is seventy, and the interview question about ten years' time becomes a joke.

truefalse.s: Jules is the founder of a company that sells furniture.
truefalse.fix: About the Fit sells clothes online, and it has grown faster than its systems.

truefalse.s: Ben is hired to work in the marketing team.
truefalse.fix: He is assigned directly to Jules, the founder, who says she has nothing for him to do.

shortAnswers.q: Ben says he wants the connection and the excitement. Why does a man with a pension want an internship rather than a job?
shortAnswers.model: He is not chasing money or status; he wants a place to go and people who need him, which retirement took away.

shortAnswers.q: Jules says she is not fun to work for. Is that honesty or a way of keeping Ben at a distance?
shortAnswers.model: It is both: she warns him honestly, but the warning also saves her from explaining why she does not want an intern in the first place.

shortAnswers.q: What is the film really saying about experience when Ben is given real work again?
shortAnswers.model: It argues that experience is not nostalgia: his value is noticing, listening and staying calm, skills the young office has forgotten how to name.

shortAnswers.q: Why does Ben keep wearing a suit in an office where nobody else does?
shortAnswers.model: The suit is his way of showing respect for the job, and the film turns it from a joke into proof that old habits can be a strength.

gaps.line: Hilly looked ___ on every woman who worked in her house.
gaps.hint: as if they were beneath her

gaps.line: Minny's mouth got her ___ trouble more than once.
For years the maids had to ___ up with whatever the white families said.
Minny finally gave Hilly a piece of her ___.
gaps.hint: told her exactly what she thought

gaps.line: For once, Aibileen refused to ___ down when Hilly threatened her.

quiz.q: Why does Aibileen finally agree to tell her story?
options: She has lost her own son and is raising another woman's child
She needs the money for her church
Skeeter threatens to publish without her
quiz.why: Grief and love have worn down her fear, and she decides that silence has already cost her too much.

quiz.q: What happens to Minny after Hilly spreads the word about her?
options: No white family will hire her until Celia does
quiz.why: Hilly's revenge keeps her out of every kitchen in town, and Celia is the only employer who does not care.

quiz.q: What does Skeeter learn about Constantine, the maid who raised her?
options: Her mother sent her away and lied about it
She died years ago in Jackson
She moved north with Skeeter's brother
quiz.why: The discovery changes how Skeeter reads her own family, and it is why the book matters to her personally.

quotes.quote: Fried chicken just tend to make you feel better about life.
quotes.note: Aibileen's voiceover, and the film's warmest line about ordinary comfort.

quotes.quote: You're a godless woman.
quotes.note: Aibileen's last words to Hilly in the driveway, after she is fired.

truefalse.s: Skeeter comes home from university with a degree and no interest in marriage.
Minny goes to work for Celia Foote after Hilly fires her.
The published book lists its author as Anonymous.
Hilly wants separate kitchens built for the maids.
truefalse.fix: She wants a separate toilet in every white house, and calls it a health measure.

truefalse.s: Skeeter's book names every maid and every family in Jackson.
truefalse.fix: The names are changed and the author is listed as Anonymous, which is the only way it can be printed.

truefalse.s: Minny is the quiet one who avoids saying what she thinks.
truefalse.fix: Minny is the most outspoken woman in Jackson, and her mouth is what gets her fired.

shortAnswers.q: Aibileen speaks one way to the Leefolt family and another way in her own kitchen. Why does she switch?
shortAnswers.model: The polite voice is a survival skill, and the switch shows what segregation costs her: she must perform a smaller self to keep her job.

shortAnswers.q: Whose book is it really: Skeeter's, Aibileen's, or all of theirs?
shortAnswers.model: It carries all three names in spirit but only Skeeter's career on the cover, which is exactly the injustice the film wants us to notice.

shortAnswers.q: Hilly says she is not a racist. Why does the film give her that line?
shortAnswers.model: Because her politeness is the mechanism of the prejudice, not its opposite; the film shows that good manners can do the same work as a sign on a door.

shortAnswers.q: Why does the film end with Aibileen walking away instead of showing us where she goes?
shortAnswers.model: The walk is the point: she has lost her job but kept her voice, and the film refuses to tidy that into a happy ending.

gaps.line: Ed told Erin to take it down a ___.
Erin would not take no for an ___.
The company tried to buy the families ___.
gaps.hint: with money, to keep them quiet

gaps.line: The numbers in the file did not ___ up.
The families in Hinkley lived hand to ___.

quiz.q: Why does Erin refuse Ed's first bonus?
options: She thinks the figure does not match the work she did
She wants to become a partner
She is leaving for another firm
quiz.why: The number is smaller than agreed, and for Erin the insult is about respect rather than money.

quiz.q: Why do the families turn against Erin before the arbitration?
options: They are told that she has sold them out
quiz.why: A letter from one plaintiff says they have been lied to, and Erin has to win their trust back one kitchen at a time.

quiz.q: What makes Charles Embry agree to make a declaration?
options: Erin lets him tell his story without pushing
He wants to be quoted in the newspaper
quiz.why: She sits with him and stays quiet, and the story of the shredded documents comes out on its own.

quotes.quote: I don't need pity. I need a paycheck.
quotes.note: Her answer when Ed apologises for losing her case, and the reason she refuses to leave without a job.

quotes.quote: It's called accountability.
quotes.note: Ed's reply when Erin says she left a message and then vanished for a week.

truefalse.s: Erin finds the medical records filed with a property sale.
Ed fires Erin for disappearing for a week, then hires her back.
More than six hundred families join the case.
The chemical in the Hinkley water is lead.
truefalse.fix: It is hexavalent chromium, which PG&E used to stop rust in its cooling towers.

truefalse.s: PG&E's first settlement offer is 333 million dollars.
truefalse.fix: The first offer is twenty million dollars; 333 million is the final settlement.

truefalse.s: Erin has a law degree but has never practised.
truefalse.fix: She has no law degree at all, and she says her brain is what she has instead.

shortAnswers.q: Erin has no law degree and no manners. Why does she succeed where trained lawyers fail?
shortAnswers.model: She treats the families as people rather than clients, so they tell her things they would never tell a lawyer in a suit.

shortAnswers.q: Whose version of the truth do you trust: the company's documents, the residents' memories, or Erin's reading of both?
shortAnswers.model: The documents are the strongest evidence, but the residents' memories tell us what the documents meant, and Erin is the one who puts the two together.

shortAnswers.q: Why does the film keep showing the babysitter, the bounced cheque and the broken car?
shortAnswers.model: The domestic detail makes the case cost something visible: every hour Erin spends in Hinkley is an hour taken from her children.

shortAnswers.q: Erin is rude and usually right. Is she a hero, or a difficult person who happens to be correct?
shortAnswers.model: The film refuses to choose: her rudeness is what makes her effective and what makes her hard to live with, and both are true.

gaps.line: Alicia stood ___ him when everyone else walked away.
Nash's idea came to him in a sudden ___ of genius.
Alicia never ___ up on him, even when the doctors had no answers.
He learned to keep the delusions at ___.
Nash ___ back into his delusions when he stopped the medication.

quiz.q: Why does Nash stop taking his medication?
options: It flattens his thinking, and he cannot work
quiz.why: The drugs dull his mind and his marriage, and he decides that thinking is the part of himself he cannot lose.

quiz.q: What makes Alicia realise that Charles is not real?
options: Marcee, the little girl, never grows older
Dr Rosen shows her the hospital file
quiz.why: She runs after Nash and sees that the child has stayed exactly the same age for years.

quiz.q: What is the turning point in Nash's treatment?
options: He learns to recognise the delusions and ignore them
He leaves Alicia and moves away
quiz.why: He cannot make the figures disappear, so he learns to test them and to live alongside them.

quotes.quote: I've always believed in numbers.
quotes.note: The opening of his Nobel speech, and the belief the film quietly tests.

quotes.quote: Find a truly original idea. It's the only way I'll ever matter.
quotes.note: His answer to the question of what he wants from Princeton.

truefalse.s: Nash's delusions include a roommate, a little girl and a government agent.
Nash wins the Nobel Prize in Economics in 1994.
Alicia is a physics student when she meets Nash.
Nash's great idea is a code-breaking machine.
truefalse.fix: His great idea is game theory, which later wins him the Nobel Prize.

truefalse.s: Nash is diagnosed with schizophrenia while he is still a student at Princeton.
truefalse.fix: He is diagnosed years later, after his marriage, when the delusions have taken hold.

truefalse.s: Alicia leaves Nash when she learns about his illness.
truefalse.fix: She stays, and the film makes her decision the centre of its second half.

shortAnswers.q: The film shows the world from inside Nash's head. Whose version of reality do you trust, and how does the film make us doubt both?
shortAnswers.model: We trust Alicia because she sees what we cannot, but the film has already taught us to believe Nash's visions, so our own judgement becomes part of the story.

shortAnswers.q: Nash learns to live with his hallucinations instead of curing them. Why is that a braver ending?
shortAnswers.model: A cure would be a miracle; living with an illness he cannot argue away is the harder and more honest victory.

shortAnswers.q: Alicia almost never raises her voice. Why does the film keep her quiet at the moment she decides to stay?
shortAnswers.model: Her quietness makes the decision look deliberate rather than dramatic, which is more frightening and more convincing than a speech.

shortAnswers.q: The film changes some facts of Nash's life. Is that a lie, or is that what fiction is for?
shortAnswers.model: It is a shaping rather than a lie: the film uses one life to say something true about illness and love, and the cost is accuracy about the details.

gaps.line: Dixon wanted to get ___ of Viktor before the inspection.
By the third month, Viktor was at his wits' ___.
Viktor ___ up for Gupta when the inspectors arrived.
Dixon pulled a few ___ to keep Viktor inside the terminal.
The whole terminal came to a ___ when Viktor refused to sign.

quiz.q: Why does Viktor refuse Dixon's offer to leave the airport quietly?
options: He would have to claim he was afraid to go home
He wants to stay in America for good
He has nowhere else to go
quiz.why: The offer depends on a lie about his country, and Viktor will not say it, even to get out.

quiz.q: How does Viktor first earn money inside the terminal?
options: By returning luggage trolleys for the coins
By cleaning the floors at night
quiz.why: He collects the abandoned trolleys and keeps the deposit coins, which is just enough to eat.

quiz.q: Why does Amelia keep coming back to the terminal?
options: She is unhappy and Viktor listens to her
She is waiting for a visa
quiz.why: She passes through every week, and Viktor is the one person who asks her nothing and listens to everything.

quotes.quote: I am from Krakozhia.
quotes.note: His answer to every official, and the one fact none of them will accept.

quotes.quote: You're a man without a country.
quotes.note: Dixon's summary of the case, said with the patience of a man reading a form.

truefalse.s: Viktor's country is called Krakozhia.
Viktor lives in the international transit lounge because he never crosses the border.
Viktor came to New York to get the last autograph for his father's collection.
Viktor's father was a jazz musician.
truefalse.fix: His father was a fan who collected the signatures of jazz musicians.

truefalse.s: Amelia is a customs officer at JFK.
truefalse.fix: She is a flight attendant who passes through the terminal every week.

truefalse.s: Viktor spends his first weeks in the terminal in a hotel room paid for by the airline.
truefalse.fix: He sleeps on a bench in the transit lounge, because he has almost no money and cannot leave.

shortAnswers.q: Viktor cannot leave the airport and cannot enter the country. Is the terminal a prison or a home?
shortAnswers.model: It becomes both: the film shows that a place can be a cage and a community at the same time, depending on who else is in it.

shortAnswers.q: Dixon says he is only following the rules. Is he a villain, or a man with a job?
shortAnswers.model: He is a bureaucrat who hides behind procedure, and the film shows that ordinary rules can do harm when nobody asks who they are hurting.

shortAnswers.q: Viktor learns English from signs and television. What does that say about how language is really learned?
shortAnswers.model: It says that need and repetition teach faster than lessons; he learns the words that let him survive, one sign at a time.

shortAnswers.q: Why does the film keep Viktor's English simple and repetitive?
shortAnswers.model: The short sentences make him sound honest and stubborn, and they let us hear the effort behind every answer.

gaps.line: Grandpa told Olive to go ___ it and ignore what anyone else thought.
The family had to ___ together every time the van broke down.
Dwayne's silence drove his family up the ___.
Grandpa never minced his ___ when he told Richard what he thought.
Dwayne finally ___ his silence in the middle of the desert.

quiz.q: Why does Richard want Olive to compete even when the family is falling apart?
options: He needs her to prove his winners-and-losers system
He has promised the pageant organisers
quiz.why: If Olive wins, his whole philosophy is right; if she does not compete, the family has lost by his own rules.

quiz.q: Why does the family run back on stage and join Olive's dance?
options: They choose her over the audience's opinion
They want to shock the judges
They are trying to stop the music
quiz.why: After a whole film of arguing, they stand with her in public, which is the only kind of love this family knows how to show.

quiz.q: Why does Olive perform the routine that Grandpa taught her?
options: It is the last thing they made together
She wants to embarrass the judges
quiz.why: Grandpa chose the music and taught her the moves, so the dance is a goodbye as much as a performance.

quotes.quote: Sarcasm is the refuge of losers.
quotes.note: Richard's line to Frank, straight out of step four of his programme.

quotes.quote: You are the most beautiful girl in the whole world.
quotes.note: Grandpa's answer when Olive asks him whether she is pretty.

truefalse.s: The family drives from Albuquerque to Redondo Beach.
Dwayne has taken a vow of silence until he gets into flight school.
The van has to be pushed to start because the clutch is broken.
Grandpa dies in a hospital in California.
truefalse.fix: He dies in his sleep at a motel on the road, before the family reaches California.

truefalse.s: Dwayne breaks his silence when he wins a place at flight school.
truefalse.fix: He breaks it when he learns that he is colour-blind and cannot fly.

truefalse.s: Olive wins the pageant.
truefalse.fix: She does not win; the family leaves with her, and the film ends on the drive home.

shortAnswers.q: Richard divides the world into winners and losers. What does the film think of that idea?
shortAnswers.model: It takes the idea seriously and then shows its cost: the people Richard loves are all, by his own measure, losers, and they are worth more than his programme.

shortAnswers.q: Olive is seven and wants to be a beauty queen. Is the film laughing at her, at the pageant, or at the adults around her?
shortAnswers.model: It laughs at the adults and at the pageant and never at Olive; her seriousness is the film's way of showing what the adults have forgotten.

shortAnswers.q: Grandpa tells Olive to do what she loves, whatever other people think. Is that good advice for a child?
shortAnswers.model: It is good advice delivered badly: the freedom is right, but a seven-year-old also needs adults who will protect her from the room.

shortAnswers.q: The family insults each other constantly and nobody leaves. Why does the film make love sound so rude?
shortAnswers.model: Because for this family insults are the only language they have left, and the film lets the shouting carry affection as well as damage.

gaps.line: Katherine had to ___ her ground in a room full of men.
Mary had to ___ the odds to get into that school.
Katherine ran ___ and forth to a bathroom in another building.
Paul Stafford tried to ___ her out of the meetings.
Mary's case ___ on an old Virginia law about segregated schools.

quiz.q: Why does Harrison tear down the bathroom sign?
options: The rule is costing him working hours and making the team look foolish
Katherine asks him to do it
A court orders him to remove it
quiz.why: He is a practical man: the runs to another building are wasting time, and the injustice only becomes visible when it slows the mission.

quiz.q: Why does Dorothy learn to program the IBM machine?
options: She sees the machine will replace her team
Harrison orders her to learn it
She wants a job as an engineer
quiz.why: She reads the manual and teaches herself so that her group still has work after the machine arrives.

quiz.q: Why does Paul Stafford dislike Katherine at first?
options: Her numbers make his own work look slow
He thinks she is a spy
quiz.why: He is used to being the cleverest person in the room, and her calculations keep arriving before his.

quotes.quote: It's not because we wear skirts. It's because we wear glasses.
quotes.note: Katherine's answer to Jim Johnson, and the film's clearest statement of what the women are hired for.

quotes.quote: Despite what you may think, I have nothing against y'all.
quotes.note: Said while she is blocking a promotion: the politeness is the point.

truefalse.s: Katherine is a computer, a woman who does the calculations by hand.
Dorothy learns FORTRAN and becomes the supervisor of the programming group.
John Glenn asks for Katherine to check the numbers before his flight.
Mary Jackson wants to become a teacher.
truefalse.fix: She wants to become an engineer, and the night classes she needs are held at a whites-only school.

truefalse.s: The IBM machine is brought in to help the women finish their work.
truefalse.fix: The IBM 7090 is brought in to replace the human computers, which is why Dorothy learns to program it.

truefalse.s: Al Harrison is the engineer who keeps Katherine out of the Space Task Group.
truefalse.fix: Harrison brings her into the group; it is Paul Stafford who keeps her out of the meetings.

shortAnswers.q: The film is called Hidden Figures. Who is hidden, and by whom?
shortAnswers.model: The women are hidden by the record and by the office itself, and the film's job is to put them back into a story that was told without them.

shortAnswers.q: Vivian Mitchell says she has nothing against you people while blocking a promotion. What does that politeness hide?
shortAnswers.model: It hides the same exclusion in a softer voice; the film shows that courtesy can be a way of refusing without having to say no.

shortAnswers.q: Katherine answers every insult with a fact. Why does she use that tone, and what does it cost her?
shortAnswers.model: Facts are the only language the room accepts from her, and the cost is that she never gets to be angry in public.

shortAnswers.q: Is Al Harrison a good man who changes, or a man who moves only when it helps the mission?
shortAnswers.model: He changes when the injustice becomes inefficient, which is a smaller kind of courage than it looks, and the film knows it.

gaps.line: The people in the farmhouse could not ___ along for one night.
By midnight the house was ___ off from the rest of the world.
Ben ___ charge while the others argued about the cellar.
Tom and Judy decided to make a ___ for it in the truck.
Everyone in the house was on ___ all night.

quiz.q: Why does Harry refuse to come out of the cellar?
options: He trusts the cellar more than Ben's plan
He is looking for his daughter
He is waiting for the rescue party
quiz.why: He is afraid of the open ground floor and will not accept a plan he did not make himself.

quiz.q: Why does Barbra barely speak in the first hour?
options: She is in shock after her brother's death
She is looking for her father
quiz.why: She has just seen her brother killed, and the film shows the shock in her silence rather than in words.

quiz.q: What goes wrong with the plan to escape in the truck?
options: The truck catches fire at the pump
quiz.why: The attempt ends in the fire at the pump, and after that the group has no plan left.

quotes.quote: We'll be safer in the cellar.
quotes.note: Harry's whole argument, and the plan that splits the house in two.

quotes.quote: The dead are returning to life.
quotes.note: The bulletin that names what the characters keep refusing to believe.

truefalse.s: The film begins in a cemetery, where Barbra and her brother visit a grave.
Ben boards up the windows while Harry argues for the cellar.
The film is shot in black and white.
The survivors are rescued at dawn by the army.
truefalse.fix: Ben is shot by a posse who mistake him for one of the dead, and the film ends with his body on a fire.

truefalse.s: Barbra escapes the farmhouse with Ben.
truefalse.fix: She never leaves the house, and Ben ends the night alone.

truefalse.s: Harry Cooper wants to make a run for the nearest town.
truefalse.fix: Harry wants everyone in the cellar; it is Ben who wants to hold the ground floor.

shortAnswers.q: The film puts strangers in one room. What does each person want, and why can't they agree?
shortAnswers.model: Each of them wants safety on their own terms, and the film shows that fear makes people defend a plan rather than listen to one.

shortAnswers.q: Is this a horror film about monsters, or about people?
shortAnswers.model: The monsters set the clock, but the horror comes from the living: who is trusted, who is listened to, and who is shot at the end.

shortAnswers.q: The news broadcasts give information in pieces. How does that shape the characters' choices?
shortAnswers.model: Half-information makes them guess and argue, which is exactly what the audience is doing too, so the film keeps us in the same fog.

shortAnswers.q: The ending is famously harsh. What is the film saying about who gets rescued?
shortAnswers.model: It says that rescue depends on being recognised as human, and Ben is not, which is the film's real subject.

gaps.line: The staff ___ along with Michael's joke because he is the boss.
Dwight ___ at the chance to run the meeting.
Michael tried to ___ the remark off as a joke.
The meeting ___ downhill in about a minute.
Michael ___ the point of the meeting completely.

quiz.q: Why does Michael decide not to tell the staff about the possible downsizing?
options: He does not want to be the boss who brings bad news on camera
He has forgotten what Jan said
Jan orders him to keep it secret
quiz.why: He wants the documentary to show him as a leader, and bad news does not fit the picture he is performing.

quiz.q: Why does Jim put Dwight's stapler in Jell-O?
options: To wind Dwight up while the cameras watch
quiz.why: It is a patient, small prank, and Jim's look at the camera shows that he knows exactly how Dwight will react.

quiz.q: What is the turning point in Michael's prank on Pam?
options: She believes she is being fired and starts to cry
quiz.why: The joke stops being funny the moment she takes it seriously, and Michael has to admit it was a prank in front of the crew.

quotes.quote: I'm a friend first, a boss second and probably an entertainer third.
quotes.note: His summary of the atmosphere he has created, said straight to camera.

quotes.quote: This is my kingdom, as far as the eye can see.
quotes.note: The tour of the office floor, and the size of his ambition.

truefalse.s: Michael has worked at Dunder Mifflin for twelve years.
Ryan arrives from a temp agency on his first day.
Jim has hidden Dwight's belongings in Jell-O more than once.
Jan tells Michael that the Stamford branch will definitely close.
truefalse.fix: She says the board has not decided, and that Michael must convince her his branch can absorb the other.

truefalse.s: Michael explains the downsizing news to the staff in the same meeting.
truefalse.fix: He keeps it to himself, and compares it to a doctor not telling a patient that he has cancer.

truefalse.s: Michael's prank on Pam is about stolen printer paper.
truefalse.fix: He accuses her of stealing Post-it Notes, then admits it was a joke.

shortAnswers.q: Michael wants the camera to see him as a good boss. Why is that funny and painful at the same time?
shortAnswers.model: Because the gap between the performance and the reality is visible in every scene, and the staff have to live inside that gap.

shortAnswers.q: The staff say nothing when Michael is embarrassing. Would you speak up in that meeting?
shortAnswers.model: Their silence is a survival strategy: the boss controls the room, and the camera makes speaking up even more expensive.

shortAnswers.q: Jim is polite to Michael and makes fun of him behind his back. Is that kind or cruel?
shortAnswers.model: It is neither: it is the small daily dishonesty that keeps an office running, and the film makes us complicit by letting us enjoy it.

shortAnswers.q: Why does the show keep cutting to characters talking to the camera?
shortAnswers.model: The talking heads let people explain themselves and expose themselves at the same time, because what they choose to say is the joke.

gaps.line: Rebecca planned to ___ the club into the ground.
Ted ___ off the journalists' jokes with a smile.
Ted ___ up for Nate in front of the whole team.
Roy tried to ___ Ted down in front of the players.
Ted took the criticism in his ___.

quiz.q: Why does Higgins look uncomfortable while Rebecca praises Ted to the press?
options: He knows her real plan and has to stand beside it
quiz.why: Higgins is the only person in the room who knows she wants the club to fail, and his face carries the lie.

quiz.q: What does Ted do when a journalist asks whether the whole thing is a joke?
options: He keeps answering politely and admits what he does not know
He walks out of the room
quiz.why: He stays warm and honest about his ignorance, which makes the room's hostility look small.

quiz.q: Why does Rebecca offer Higgins a promotion?
options: She needs his full support for her plan
She wants him to leave the club
quiz.why: She buys his loyalty with a title and a raise, because her plan only works if he keeps quiet.

quotes.quote: Ted Lasso is gonna help me burn it to the ground.
quotes.note: Said to Higgins after the press conference: the owner's real plan in one line.

quotes.quote: I do love a locker room. Smells like potential.
quotes.note: His first visit to the dressing room, and the whole method in two sentences.

truefalse.s: Rebecca fires the previous manager in the opening scene.
Ted's last job was coaching American football at Wichita State.
Nate is the kit man, and Ted asks his name.
Rebecca tells the journalists that she hired Ted because he is a proven coach.
truefalse.fix: In public she calls it a fresh start; in private she tells Higgins she wants to burn the club down.

truefalse.s: Ted tells the press that he has coached Premier League football before.
truefalse.fix: He admits that he has never coached the sport they call football at any level.

truefalse.s: Ted's press conference goes badly because he refuses to answer questions.
truefalse.fix: He answers happily but gets the game wrong, saying four quarters and being corrected to two halves.

shortAnswers.q: Rebecca hires Ted for a reason she keeps to herself. Is she a villain, a businesswoman, or something more complicated?
shortAnswers.model: She is a woman using the only power she has to hurt the man who hurt her, and the film makes her sympathetic without excusing it.

shortAnswers.q: Ted knows almost nothing about football. Could not knowing the rules ever make a coach better?
shortAnswers.model: It can, because he sees the people rather than the tactics, and the players have been coached by experts for years without being seen.

shortAnswers.q: Ted asks Nate his name, and Nate says nobody ever does. Why does that small moment matter?
shortAnswers.model: It shows that Ted's method is attention rather than knowledge, and it is the first proof that he might be good at the job.

shortAnswers.q: Why does Ted answer every hostile question with a joke and a compliment?
shortAnswers.model: The jokes keep him in control of the room without a fight, and they buy him time to work out what he actually thinks.

gaps.line: Jake was ___ on winning the bet from the first minute.
The squad was ___ aback by Holt's first order.
Amy ___ her nose up at Jake's shortcuts.
Boyle could not ___ up the courage to ask Rosa out.
The bet got out of ___ by the end of the day.

quiz.q: Why does Amy make the bet with Jake?
options: She wants to prove that proper police work beats his shortcuts
She wants a date with him
quiz.why: Jake's success without paperwork offends her sense of the job, and the bet is her chance to prove that method matters.

quiz.q: Why does Jake take the bet instead of ignoring it?
options: He cannot resist proving he is the better detective
quiz.why: The bet is not really about the date: it is about being told, again, that he is not good enough.

quiz.q: What is the turning point for Jake and Holt?
options: Holt tells him something personal in the car and Jake listens
quiz.why: The captain offers a fact about himself instead of a rule, and Jake has to decide whether to make a joke of it.

quotes.quote: I need my rabbi.
quotes.note: Jake's word for the mentor he wants in a captain, said before he has met one.

quotes.quote: Catch bad guys and look good doing it.
quotes.note: His summary of the job at the end of the arrest, tie and all.

truefalse.s: Jake finds the camera hidden inside a teddy bear.
Terry is on administrative leave because he is afraid of getting hurt.
Jake is sent to the records room after Ratko escapes.
Holt's first order is that the detectives must wear uniforms.
truefalse.fix: He asks for a necktie, not a uniform, though Jake works out that the tie is about being part of a team.

truefalse.s: The bet is about who can close more cases this month.
truefalse.fix: It is about who makes more arrests this year, with a car and a date as the prizes.

truefalse.s: Holt was given his own command as soon as he made captain.
truefalse.fix: He was put in a public affairs unit for years and only now has a command of his own.

shortAnswers.q: Jake is a great detective and a terrible adult. Can someone be excellent at their job and still be a problem?
shortAnswers.model: Yes, and the film is careful to show both: his arrests are real, and so is the cost to everyone who has to work with him.

shortAnswers.q: Holt makes Jake wear a tie. Is that about discipline, respect, or power?
shortAnswers.model: It is about all three at once, and Jake only understands it when he sees that Holt was kept off the team for years.

shortAnswers.q: Amy and Jake bet a car against a date. Is that competitive fun or something less healthy?
shortAnswers.model: The film plays it as fun, but the stakes are uneven: one prize is an object and the other is a person, and Amy knows it.

shortAnswers.q: Holt speaks in full sentences and never uses contractions. Why does the show give him that voice?
shortAnswers.model: It makes him sound like the rules themselves, and it makes the moment he speaks personally in the car land much harder.
